hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative agreement to extend ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for an additional two months and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the White House confirmed. The arrangement requires President Trump's approval before taking effect.

The deal involves a 60-day memorandum of understanding between the two countries. The agreement comes as the conflict has driven up energy prices and created economic pressures for American households.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, has been a focal point of tensions during the conflict. Reopening the passage would ease pressure on energy markets and reduce costs for consumers facing high gas prices. Oil prices fell following reports of the breakthrough in negotiations.

The tentative framework represents progress after weeks of escalating tensions and failed peace talks. Pakistan's army chief traveled to Tehran to continue mediation efforts, with a second round of negotiations expected to take place in Islamabad. Pakistan's prime minister also embarked on a four-day tour of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to coordinate support from regional powers for peace efforts.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the administration remained "very much engaged in these negotiations" and felt "good about the prospects of a deal." She emphasized that "nothing is official until you hear it from us here at the White House."

Both sides had expressed interest in prolonging the truce. Sources in Tehran indicated Iran had demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for another round of negotiations with the US. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the military would continue operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

The ceasefire extension would provide additional time for diplomatic negotiations while reducing immediate military risks. During the extended period, the memorandum establishes parameters for both countries' actions.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated the administration was prepared to escalate financial pressure on Iran through secondary sanctions if negotiations failed. The US military had implemented a naval blockade of Iranian ports, turning back nine ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, including a Chinese-owned tanker now under US sanctions.

Iran's military leadership warned it could halt trade in the Gulf region if the US did not lift its blockade. Trump claimed he had won agreement from Chinese President Xi Jinping not to send arms to Iran, though China's foreign ministry had previously denied supplying weapons.

The agreement's success depends on President Trump's final decision. Administration officials have not provided a timeline for when the president will review and potentially approve the framework.

Energy markets have reacted positively to news of the potential agreement, though prices remain elevated compared to pre-conflict levels.

cards.headline: Iran launches missile toward Kuwait in retaliation for US strikes
cards.teaser: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted an unspecified US base after earlier American strikes.
cards.body:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched a ballistic missile targeting a US military base, according to the country's military. The US military confirmed the strike was directed toward Kuwait. Iran said the attack was in response to earlier American strikes.

The escalation threatens ongoing diplomatic efforts between the two countries. Negotiations are underway to extend a fragile ceasefire and initiate nuclear talks aimed at ending the three-month conflict. Reports of a potential extended ceasefire have already influenced global markets, with oil prices falling on expectations of progress in peace discussions.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Beirut for first time in weeks
cards.teaser: The Israeli military launched what it called a targeted strike on the Lebanese capital.
cards.body:
Israel struck Beirut in a targeted operation, the first attack on the Lebanese capital in weeks. The city had previously been largely spared from Israeli attacks despite both Israel and Hezbollah trading accusations about violations of last month's ceasefire agreement.

The strike could undermine ongoing diplomatic efforts by the United States and Iran to negotiate a peace agreement regarding the conflict in Iran. Israel has intensified its offensive operations in Lebanon in recent days.

cards.headline: Gaza hospitals report deaths in Israeli strike targeting Hamas commander
cards.teaser: At least five children were reportedly killed in the attack.
cards.body:
Hamas said Mohammed Odeh, the head of its military wing, was killed in an Israeli strike on a residential building in Gaza City. His wife and two children also died in the attack.

Hospitals in Gaza reported that at least five children were killed overall in the strike. Israel has continued its military operations across the region, including targeting Hamas leaders.

cards.headline: Consumer spending outpaces income growth as households draw down savings
cards.teaser: Americans are spending faster than their income is growing, drawing on savings to maintain consumption as energy prices rise.
cards.body:
Americans are spending at a rate that exceeds their income growth, increasingly relying on savings to support their purchases as the energy shock from the Iran war affects household budgets. The trend represents a shift in how consumers are managing their finances amid rising costs.

Consumer spending has remained steady despite low sentiment readings among households. Data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis shows the gap between spending and income growth is widening, creating questions about the sustainability of current consumption patterns as prices continue rising faster than household earnings.

cards.headline: Senator calls ad tech industry a national security threat after troops targeted with location data
cards.body:
The U.S. government confirmed that American troops were targeted using location data, prompting a leading privacy lawmaker to call for treating the ad tech industry as a national security threat.

The disclosure marks a significant escalation in concerns about how commercially available location information can be weaponized against military personnel. Location data collected through smartphone apps and other digital services can reveal the movements and positions of service members, potentially exposing them to foreign adversaries.

The senator's statement represents one of the strongest warnings yet from Congress about the national security risks posed by the data broker and advertising technology ecosystem. Companies routinely collect, buy, and sell location information gathered from millions of devices, often with minimal oversight or restrictions on how that data can be used.

The ad tech industry operates by tracking users across websites and apps to serve targeted advertisements. This tracking generates detailed profiles that include location history, browsing habits, and other personal information. While the practice is common in commercial advertising, national security officials have grown increasingly worried about adversaries purchasing this data to identify and track government employees, military personnel, and intelligence officers.

The call to treat the industry as a security threat could signal forthcoming legislative action to restrict how location data can be collected, sold, and used. Previous attempts to regulate data brokers have faced resistance from industry groups arguing that such restrictions would harm legitimate business operations and advertising effectiveness.

No details were provided about when the targeting occurred, which troops were affected, or which adversaries may have accessed the location data. The confirmation itself, however, validates long-standing warnings from privacy advocates and security experts that the unrestricted sale of location information poses risks beyond consumer privacy concerns.

The statement comes as lawmakers in both parties have shown growing interest in data privacy legislation, though disagreements over federal versus state regulatory authority have stalled comprehensive reform efforts. The national security angle may provide new momentum for restrictions specifically targeting location data sales.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister calls for new relationship with US in New York speech
cards.teaser: Mark Carney said Canada's distancing from the US is beneficial for Americans.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. Carney emphasized the need for a "true partnership" that would reimagine cooperation between the two countries in sectors facing global competitive challenges.

The speech focused on greater economic cooperation between the neighboring nations, with Carney framing the proposed relationship as a way to strengthen both countries moving forward.

cards.headline: 16 students die in Kenya school fire
cards.teaser: Parents waited roughly 12 hours after the fire for news of their children.
cards.body:
A fire swept through a dormitory at Utumishi girls academy in Gilgil, Nakuru county, killing at least 16 students. The blaze broke out just after midnight at the school, located about 76 miles north-west of Nairobi in Kenya's Rift Valley.

Parents faced an anxious wait for updates on their children in the hours following the fire. The incident has renewed concerns about safety standards at Kenyan schools.

cards.headline: Gaza hospitals report deaths in Israeli strike targeting Hamas commander
cards.teaser: At least five children were reportedly killed in the attack.
cards.body:
Hamas said Mohammed Odeh, the head of its military wing, was killed in an Israeli strike on a residential building in Gaza City. His wife and two children also died in the attack.

Hospitals in Gaza reported that at least five children were killed overall in the strike. Israel has continued its military operations across the region, including targeting Hamas leaders.

cards.headline: Portugal sets hottest May day on record as Europe faces heatwave
cards.teaser: Red alerts have been issued in Italy while French students take exams in overheated schools.
cards.body:
Portugal broke its record for the hottest day ever recorded in May as a heatwave swept across Europe. The extreme temperatures affected multiple countries on the continent.

French students took exams in schools with high temperatures. Red weather alerts were issued in Italy as the heatwave continued.

cards.headline: Man arrested after stabbing at Swiss train station injures three
cards.teaser: A 31-year-old Swiss man was taken into custody following the incident.
cards.body:
Three people were injured in a stabbing incident at a Swiss train station. A 31-year-old Swiss man has been arrested in connection with the attack.

Police secured the area following the incident, with parts of the station cordoned off as shown in images from the scene.

cards.teaser: Mark Carney said Canada's distancing from the US is beneficial for Americans.

hero.headline: Supreme Court rules for Mississippi death row inmate who alleged racial bias in jury selection
hero.body:
The US Supreme Court has ruled in favor of Terry Pitchford, a Black man convicted of capital murder and currently on death row in Mississippi, who claimed that racial bias affected his jury composition. The justices sided with Pitchford in a 5-4 decision on Thursday.

Pitchford, who was 18 years old when convicted of murder, argued that Black jurors were improperly excluded from his trial. His legal challenge centered on whether prosecutors engaged in race-based discrimination during jury selection, a practice that has faced increasing legal scrutiny in capital punishment cases.

The decision represents a significant ruling on jury composition and constitutional protections against racial discrimination in the legal system. By voting in Pitchford's favor, the Supreme Court found merit in his allegations that the jury selection process violated his constitutional rights.

This ruling comes as part of a broader national conversation about fairness in death penalty cases. Historically, capital punishment has faced criticism regarding potential racial bias in how juries are assembled, particularly when Black defendants are on trial. Legal experts have long pointed out that the composition of juries can substantially affect trial outcomes and whether defendants receive fair proceedings.

The Supreme Court's decision reinforces existing legal protections designed to prevent race from becoming a factor in determining jury membership in criminal trials. The case reflects ongoing examination of how race has influenced the American criminal justice system throughout its history.

The ruling may have wider implications for other death row cases where similar claims of racial discrimination in jury selection have been raised. The decision could prompt reviews of other cases where comparable allegations were made but not fully addressed or resolved by lower courts. Defense attorneys representing death row inmates may now point to this precedent when challenging jury composition in their own appeals.

The justices' 5-4 vote margin indicates that the decision was closely contested, suggesting that the court remains divided on issues related to race and the criminal justice system. Such narrow majorities in cases involving racial discrimination claims demonstrate the contentious nature of these legal questions.

Pitchford's case illustrates the persistent challenges that defendants face when challenging jury selection practices. The lengthy legal process that brought his case before the Supreme Court reflects the complexity of proving racial bias in jury selection and the multiple appeals required in capital cases.

The ruling provides a legal framework for evaluating future claims of racial discrimination during jury selection. It underscores the Supreme Court's commitment to addressing racial bias in the judicial process, though the narrow vote suggests continued disagreement among justices about how these protections should be applied in practice.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation involving E. Jean Carroll testimony in Trump case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has launched a criminal probe related to testimony given by E. Jean Carroll in her sexual abuse lawsuit against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll's testimony in her civil lawsuit against former President Donald Trump. The probe centers on whether Carroll made false statements about funding she received for the case.

Federal prosecutors in Chicago are handling the investigation. Carroll won her civil lawsuit against Trump, with a jury finding in her favor on sexual abuse allegations.

cards.headline: Federal judge declines to block Trump order limiting mail-in voting
cards.teaser: A federal judge refused to stop a Trump executive order that places restrictions on voting by mail, though the ruling has no immediate effect on upcoming midterm elections.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. has declined to temporarily block President Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The decision allows the order to remain in effect while legal challenges continue. Another judge may rule on the order soon.

Democrats had sought an injunction to prevent implementation of the restrictions on mail-in ballots in federal elections. The judge's ruling represents a setback for those efforts to halt the order.

cards.headline: Protesters and ICE agents clash outside New Jersey detention center during hunger strike
cards.teaser: Tensions erupted between demonstrators and Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents at Delaney Hall in Newark as detainees staged a hunger strike.
cards.body:
Protesters and ICE agents clashed outside a detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, as tensions escalated during an ongoing hunger strike by detainees at Delaney Hall. The confrontations included physical altercations, with ICE agents deploying pepper spray against demonstrators who blocked vehicles.

The protests occurred as detainees inside the facility, operated by the GEO Group, refused meals to draw attention to conditions at the center. Demonstrators gathered outside to support the hunger strikers, leading to the confrontations with federal immigration enforcement personnel. Protesters blocked ICE vehicles during the demonstrations.

cards.headline: Two boys die in separate water incidents during UK heatwave
cards.teaser: A boy's body was recovered from a pond in Kent and another teenager died in the River Thames in Oxford in the latest heatwave-related drownings.
cards.body:
Two boys have died in separate water incidents during the UK heatwave. One boy's body was recovered from a pond in Kent, while another teenager died in the River Thames in Oxford.

These deaths are part of a broader pattern of drownings across Britain. Water safety experts have warned of the dangers as people seek relief from soaring temperatures by swimming in open water. Emergency services have reported at least nine water-related deaths in recent days, with seven involving young people. Rivers, lakes, ponds and reservoirs pose particular risks during hot weather due to unpredictable conditions and the difficulty of rescue operations.

cards.headline: Australian woman charged with traveling to Syria to join Islamic State
cards.teaser: An Australian woman faces charges for allegedly traveling to Syria to join the Islamic State, eight months after returning from Lebanon with her children.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with traveling to Syria to join the Islamic State. She returned to Australia from Lebanon several months before her arrest, accompanied by her children.

The charges relate to her alleged involvement with the Islamic State during her time in Syria. Under Australian law, citizens are prohibited from traveling to join designated terrorist organizations.

cards.headline: Man dies after being hit by train following escape from police vehicle
cards.teaser: A man was killed by a train in Hertfordshire after escaping from a vehicle while being transported to court by police.
cards.body:
A man died after being struck by a train in Hertfordshire following his escape from a police vehicle that was transporting him to court. The incident occurred while the individual was in police custody en route to a court appearance.

Hertfordshire Police have referred the case to the Independent Office for Police Conduct, the agency that investigates incidents involving law enforcement in England and Wales. The referral is standard procedure when someone dies during or following police contact.

hero.headline: Google Employee Charged With Using Internal Search Data to Win $1.2 Million in Prediction Market Bets
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors charged a Google employee with using confidential company search data to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform, generating $1.2 million in profits.

The employee accessed internal Google search data and used that information to make bets on Polymarket, according to the charges. Prosecutors allege the individual exploited insider access to information not available to the public to gain an advantage in placing wagers on the platform.

Polymarket allows users to bet on the outcomes of future events, from elections to entertainment awards. The platform has grown in popularity as a way to aggregate public predictions about real-world events. Users who correctly predict outcomes can profit from their wagers.

The case marks a significant enforcement action against insider trading in prediction markets. While insider trading laws have long applied to traditional securities markets, their application to newer platforms like prediction markets represents an expansion of how prosecutors view market manipulation.

The charges specify that the Google employee made $1.2 million through the scheme. Prosecutors did not disclose how long the alleged activity took place or what specific types of bets the individual placed using the confidential search data.

Google has not publicly commented on the charges or whether the employee remains with the company. The Department of Justice brought the case, signaling federal interest in policing fairness in prediction markets as they become more mainstream.

Prediction markets operate on the principle that aggregated public bets can serve as accurate forecasts of future events. The integrity of these platforms depends on participants having equal access to information. When insiders use confidential data unavailable to other bettors, it undermines the fairness that makes prediction markets function as forecasting tools.

The case raises questions about how companies with vast troves of internal data protect that information from misuse by employees. Search data in particular can offer insights into public interest and behavior patterns that could prove valuable for betting on future events.

cards.headline: CVS Restores Coverage for Eli Lilly Obesity Drug Zepbound After Patient Backlash
cards.teaser: The pharmacy benefits manager reversed its decision to drop coverage of the weight loss medication following complaints from patients.
cards.body:
CVS Caremark reversed its decision to drop coverage for Zepbound, Eli Lilly's obesity medication, following patient complaints. The pharmacy benefit manager has restored the drug to its formulary and added Eli Lilly's obesity pill to its coverage plans.

The move comes after patients lost access to the treatment when CVS initially removed it from coverage. Following the announcement of the expanded coverage, shares in Eli Lilly rose.

cards.headline: EU Fines Temu $200 Million for Allowing Sale of Illegal Products
cards.teaser: The European Commission penalized the Chinese-owned retailer for failing to address risks from unsafe goods sold on its platform.
cards.body:
The European Commission has fined Temu €200 million for failing to prevent the sale of illegal and dangerous products on its platform. A 19-month investigation found that consumers were very likely to encounter unsafe items, including baby toys and faulty chargers, when shopping on the Chinese-owned website.

The penalty reflects EU regulators' concerns about the retailer's inadequate risk management practices. The fine represents a significant enforcement action targeting the fast-growing e-commerce company's operations in European markets.

cards.headline: Outdoor Apparel Firm Patagonia Sues Drag Performer Pattie Gonia for Trademark Infringement
cards.teaser: The company claims the drag queen broke an agreement not to use its branding in merchandise.
cards.body:
Patagonia filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against drag performer Pattie Gonia, claiming the entertainer violated an agreement by using the company's branding on merchandise. The outdoor apparel firm took legal action over the alleged breach of their arrangement.

Pattie Gonia, an Oregon-based drag queen whose stage name combines Patagonia with a drag persona, is known for environmental activism and outdoor-themed performances. The performer has responded to the lawsuit.

cards.headline: Nick Bilton Named Executive Producer of CBS 60 Minutes as Network Fires Two Correspondents
cards.teaser: CBS editor in chief Bari Weiss tapped the tech journalist and filmmaker to lead the news program in a major restructuring.
cards.body:
Bari Weiss, CBS's editor in chief, has appointed Nick Bilton, a technology journalist and filmmaker, as executive producer of 60 Minutes. The move comes as the network declines to renew the contract of veteran correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi for the show's upcoming 59th season.

Alfonsi accused CBS News of penalizing her for refusing to compromise factual reporting. She had been at the center of controversy after Weiss shelved a segment she reported on a prison in El Salvador, which Alfonsi described as an example of "corporate meddling" at the network.

cards.headline: Trump Refiles $10 Billion Defamation Lawsuit Against Wall Street Journal
cards.teaser: The former president filed a new version of his suit after a judge dismissed an earlier complaint about an article regarding Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
Donald Trump's legal team has refiled a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal after a Florida judge dismissed an earlier version of the case. The lawsuit centers on a Wall Street Journal article about an alleged letter Trump sent to Jeffrey Epstein in 2003, which the newspaper described as "bawdy." Trump's legal team claims the reporting tarnished his reputation by describing the card as bearing his signature.

The refiled case restarts litigation that pits the U.S. president against Rupert Murdoch, who owns the Wall Street Journal. Trump has pursued multiple defamation cases against media outlets in recent years.

cards.headline: Report Warns 1.25 Million Young People in UK Could Be Out of Work or Education by 2031
cards.teaser: A study projects rising numbers of 16 to 24-year-olds not in employment, education, or training over the next five years.
cards.body:
A new report predicts that 1.25 million young people aged 16 to 24 will be out of work, education, or training by 2031. The study describes this as a "lost generation," warning that opportunities are shrinking for too many young people in this age group.

Young job seekers have reported facing significant challenges when searching for employment. Some have applied for hundreds of roles in their efforts to secure work, highlighting the difficult job market young people currently navigate.

cards.headline: Illinois passes AI safety law despite federal deregulation push
cards.teaser: Anthropic and OpenAI backed the state legislation requiring safety testing.
cards.body:
Illinois has enacted legislation requiring safety testing for artificial intelligence development, advancing state-level AI regulation as federal oversight remains uncertain. The law secured support from major AI companies Anthropic and OpenAI, helping Illinois avoid the industry opposition that has blocked similar measures in other states.

This represents a significant shift in how states are governing AI development independently of federal action.

cards.headline: Anthropic releases Opus 4.8 with tool for coordinating multiple AI agents
cards.teaser: The new model includes Dynamic Workflows for managing swarms of subagents.
cards.body:
Anthropic released Opus 4.8, its newest AI model, featuring a tool called Dynamic Workflows designed to coordinate multiple AI subagents working together. The capability allows the model to manage swarms of smaller agents operating on different tasks.

The release continues the rapid pace of large language model development among leading AI companies. Dynamic Workflows represents an architectural approach where a primary model orchestrates multiple specialized agents rather than handling all tasks through a single system.

cards.headline: Waymo launches Chinese-made robotaxi now accepting riders
cards.teaser: The Ojai minivan robotaxi arrives as Waymo faces operational challenges.
cards.body:
Waymo is now accepting passengers in its new Ojai robotaxi, a Chinese-manufactured minivan based on the Zeekr RT. The company will initially offer free rides to select passengers in San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix, with plans to gradually expand to additional riders and cities.

The Ojai represents Waymo's first publicly available autonomous vehicle built specifically for commercial robotaxi service rather than retrofitted from a consumer model. The launch comes after several months of testing and follows years of development.

cards.headline: Steam Deck sells out in North America after 40 percent price increase
cards.teaser: Valve's handheld gaming device sold out within 24 hours despite higher prices.
cards.body:
The Steam Deck sold out across North America within 24 hours of returning to stock, even after Valve increased prices by more than 40 percent. The company attributed the price increase to rising component costs, though the device itself remained unchanged.

The immediate sellout demonstrates strong ongoing demand for handheld PC gaming despite the substantial cost increase. The Steam Deck remains available in Europe, Australia, and Asia.

cards.headline: Insurance tech startup Corgi raises $106 million at doubled valuation
cards.teaser: The Series B1 round values Corgi at $2.6 billion, three weeks after its Series B.
cards.body:
Corgi, an insurance technology company, raised $106 million in a Series B1 funding round that values the startup at $2.6 billion. The valuation is double what the company achieved just three weeks earlier when it announced a $160 million Series B.

The rapid valuation increase is unusual, even in the fast-moving startup fundraising environment. The back-to-back raises suggest strong investor demand for Corgi's insurance technology platform, though the company has not disclosed specific details about what drove the additional funding or valuation jump.

cards.headline: Musk contradicts SpaceX filing on length of Anthropic compute deal
cards.teaser: The CEO characterized the arrangement as short-term despite company documents indicating payments through 2029.
cards.body:
Elon Musk publicly described xAI's compute deal with Anthropic as short-term and cancellable, contradicting SpaceX's own S-1 filing that outlined payments extending through May 2029. The discrepancy has raised questions about the actual terms of the arrangement.

SpaceX filed the S-1 document as part of regulatory requirements, making the payment timeline through 2029 part of the official record. Musk's characterization of the deal as brief and flexible conflicts with that disclosure.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup winner during his NHL career, has died at age 60, the NHL Alumni Association announced Thursday.

Lemieux's 21-season professional hockey career spanned from 1983 to 2009 and included championships with three different franchises. He won his first Stanley Cup with the Montreal Canadiens in 1986, followed by back-to-back titles with the New Jersey Devils in 1995 and the Colorado Avalanche in 1996. He secured his fourth championship with New Jersey again in 2000.

The right winger was selected 26th overall by Montreal in the 1983 NHL Draft. He made an immediate contribution to the Canadiens organization and became known for his physical style of play and strong postseason performance throughout his career.

During his regular season play, Lemieux registered 379 goals and 406 assists across 1,215 games. His playoff record stood out notably, with 80 goals in 234 postseason contests. In 1995, he won the Conn Smythe Trophy as the playoff MVP when he helped lead the Devils to their first Stanley Cup championship.

Over the course of his career, Lemieux played for eight different teams. In addition to the Canadiens, Devils, and Avalanche, he also wore uniforms for the Phoenix Coyotes, Dallas Stars, San Jose Sharks, and Philadelphia Flyers.

Following his retirement from professional hockey in 2009, Lemieux remained involved with the sport through the NHL Alumni Association, which provides support to former players. He also participated in community activities and alumni events.

Lemieux left behind a legacy that places him among a select group of players who won multiple Stanley Cup championships with different organizations. His combination of aggressive play and playoff success made him both a feared competitor and a valued teammate during his time in the league.

His son, Brendan Lemieux, has continued the family's hockey tradition by playing in the NHL. The family has survived him following his death at age 60.

cards.headline: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner loses in French Open second round
cards.teaser: World number one Jannik Sinner dropped 18 of the final 20 games in a second-round exit at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Top seed Jannik Sinner has been eliminated from the French Open in the second round, falling to 56th-ranked Juan Manuel Cerundolo of Argentina in a five-set match. The upset marked a significant disappointment for the Italian player, who had been seeking to win his first French Open title.

Sinner's performance deteriorated sharply during the match, losing 18 of the final 20 games after coming close to victory. The loss was compounded by an injury that hampered his play throughout the contest.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart addresses team after Trump event
cards.teaser: Dart spoke with Giants teammates during a team meeting about his introduction of President Trump at a New York event.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart held a team meeting Wednesday to discuss his recent introduction of President Donald Trump at a New York event. According to sources who spoke with ESPN and NFL Network, Dart addressed his teammates directly during the session about his appearance at the Trump event.

The meeting came in response to attention generated by Dart's role introducing the president at the gathering the previous week.

cards.headline: Shohei Ohtani hits home run in Dodgers combined no-hitter bid
cards.teaser: Ohtani hit a leadoff home run as the Dodgers positioned themselves for a combined no-hitter Wednesday night.
cards.body:
Shohei Ohtani launched a leadoff home run Wednesday night as the Los Angeles Dodgers worked toward a combined no-hitter. The offensive spark helped position the team for the pitching achievement.

Despite the home run and the Dodgers' no-hit bid, Ohtani was critical of his own play, lamenting flaws in his performance during the game.

cards.headline: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino speaks with AC Milan about vacancy
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team coach has discussed the Italian club's open head coaching position.
cards.body:
Mauricio Pochettino, head coach of the United States men's national team, is in talks with AC Milan about the Serie A club's vacant managerial position. The discussions represent broader interest in Pochettino's services beyond his current role with the USMNT.

The timing comes as the US national team opens its World Cup camp following the squad announcement. Italian journalist Nicolò Schira first reported the Milan discussions, which have since been confirmed by multiple sources.

cards.headline: Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq has hernia surgery
cards.teaser: First-round pick underwent a minor procedure but is expected to be ready for training camp.
cards.body:
New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq underwent hernia surgery Thursday, according to head coach Aaron Glenn. The procedure was described as minor.

Glenn said Sadiq is expected to be ready for training camp, which begins later this summer. The timeline should allow the first-round draft pick sufficient recovery time before the start of the season.

cards.headline: Canadiens face elimination after 4-0 home loss to Carolina
cards.teaser: Montreal lost Game 4 at home and now must win multiple games to avoid playoff elimination.
cards.body:
The Montreal Canadiens suffered a 4-0 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 4 at home, putting them in an elimination situation with multiple games still required to reach the offseason. The defeat marked a complete no-show for Montreal in front of their home crowd.

Montreal has faced elimination scenarios during these playoffs before, but never with several games standing between them and the end of their season. The Canadiens described themselves as super underdogs following the shutout loss.

hero.headline: Netflix Feature Animation Workers Ratify First Union Contract
hero.body:
Netflix Animation Studios feature production workers have voted to ratify their first union contract with The Animation Guild, the union representing animation workers in the industry. The contract passed with 89 percent support.

The agreement establishes wage minimums for production workers at the streaming company's animation division. It also includes dismissal pay provisions and workplace protections that had not previously existed for these employees.

The Animation Guild, officially known as IATSE Local 839, represents workers across the animation industry. The contract covers production workers involved in feature animation projects at Netflix.

The ratification represents a shift in labor organization at major streaming platforms. Netflix has expanded its animation output in recent years, producing both feature films and series for its global subscriber base.

Production workers at animation studios typically handle coordination, scheduling, and administrative tasks that support the creative process. The new contract formalizes their employment terms and establishes baseline standards for compensation and job security.

The overwhelming vote in favor suggests broad support among affected workers for union representation. Nearly nine out of ten voting members approved the contract terms negotiated between the company and the guild.

Streaming companies have faced increasing pressure from workers seeking union representation across various departments. Animation workers at other studios have also organized in recent years, though not all efforts have resulted in contracts.

The agreement applies specifically to feature production staff rather than animators or other creative roles, which may have separate representation or employment structures. Netflix operates multiple animation initiatives across different formats and age groups.

The contract terms were not detailed in the announcement beyond wage minimums, dismissal pay, and workplace protections. The guild did not specify the duration of the agreement or when the new terms take effect.

cards.headline: Tom Hardy in Talks to Return to MobLand After Exit Reports
cards.teaser: The actor was not fired from the Paramount Plus series, and producers are working to bring him back for a third season.
cards.body:
Tom Hardy has not been fired from MobLand, according to Variety. Despite reports last week suggesting he would exit the Paramount Plus series before a third season, sources have confirmed that discussions are underway for his return.

The actor portrays gangster Harry Da Souza in the show. Producers are actively working through creative solutions to bring Hardy back to the cast.

cards.headline: Young MC Says Freedom 250 Event Involved Undisclosed Political Ties
cards.teaser: The rapper said artists were not informed about political involvement with the event before the lineup was announced.
cards.body:
Young MC said artists booked for the Freedom 250 event were not told about political involvement before the lineup became public. The rapper characterized the situation as a bait and switch.

The Freedom 250 controversy centers on undisclosed affiliations that artists say they were not made aware of when they agreed to perform. Young MC addressed the issue publicly, stating that performers lacked key information about the event's nature when they committed to appearing.

cards.headline: Roger Daltrey Playing More Solo Dates Than Who's Farewell Tour
cards.teaser: The 82-year-old singer said he has no plans to stop performing, despite the Who's recent North American farewell tour.
cards.body:
Roger Daltrey is performing more dates on his solo tour than the Who completed during their North American farewell tour. At 82 years old, the singer remains committed to touring and shows no signs of slowing down.

In a wide-ranging interview, Daltrey discussed his solo career, the Who's future, the band's drummer changes, and their history of smashing guitars on stage.

cards.headline: UTA Signs Outdoor Lifestyle Creator Steven Rinella and MeatEater
cards.teaser: The agency will represent the influencer and his multiplatform media company across various business areas.
cards.body:
UTA has signed Steven Rinella and his outdoor lifestyle media company MeatEater for representation. Rinella is an influential creator in the outdoor and hunting space.

MeatEater, founded in 1999, operates across video, podcasts, publishing, commerce, and live events. The company has grown into a diversified media operation focused on outdoor lifestyle content. UTA will represent both Rinella individually and the broader MeatEater business.

cards.headline: Hallie Jackson Expands Role Across NBC News Platforms
cards.teaser: The anchor will add new responsibilities while continuing her streaming show and Sunday evening news duties.
cards.body:
Hallie Jackson is expanding her presence at NBC News starting this week. The Washington-based journalist currently hosts a two-hour streaming program called Hallie Jackson Now on NBC News Now and anchors NBC Nightly News on Sundays.

Jackson's new responsibilities begin on a date specified as next week in the announcement. The expansion represents NBC News' effort to integrate its streaming operations more closely with its linear television programming.

cards.headline: Off Campus Season 2 Will Center on Allie and Dean
cards.teaser: The Amazon Prime romance series will focus on the fan-favorite couple when it returns.
cards.body:
The second season of Off Campus will focus on characters Allie and Dean. The Amazon Prime romance series does not have an official return date.

Viewers of the show have responded positively to the couple. The production confirmed that the pair will be in the spotlight when the series comes back for its next season.

hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative agreement to extend ceasefire
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for an additional two months and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the White House confirmed. The arrangement requires President Trump's approval before taking effect.

The deal involves a 60-day memorandum of understanding between the two countries. The agreement comes as the conflict has driven up energy prices and created economic pressures for American households.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments, has been a focal point of tensions during the conflict. Reopening the passage would ease pressure on energy markets and reduce costs for consumers facing high gas prices. Oil prices fell following reports of the breakthrough in negotiations.

The tentative framework represents progress after weeks of escalating tensions and failed peace talks. Pakistan's army chief traveled to Tehran to continue mediation efforts, with a second round of negotiations expected to take place in Islamabad. Pakistan's prime minister also embarked on a four-day tour of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey to coordinate support from regional powers for peace efforts.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the administration remained "very much engaged in these negotiations" and felt "good about the prospects of a deal." She emphasized that "nothing is official until you hear it from us here at the White House."

Both sides had expressed interest in prolonging the truce. Sources in Tehran indicated Iran had demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for another round of negotiations with the US. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the military would continue operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

The ceasefire extension would provide additional time for diplomatic negotiations while reducing immediate military risks. During the extended period, the memorandum establishes parameters for both countries' actions.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated the administration was prepared to escalate financial pressure on Iran through secondary sanctions if negotiations failed. The US military had implemented a naval blockade of Iranian ports, turning back nine ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, including a Chinese-owned tanker now under US sanctions.

Iran's military leadership warned it could halt trade in the Gulf region if the US did not lift its blockade. Trump claimed he had won agreement from Chinese President Xi Jinping not to send arms to Iran, though China's foreign ministry had previously denied supplying weapons.

The agreement's success depends on President Trump's final decision. Administration officials have not provided a timeline for when the president will review and potentially approve the framework.

Energy markets have reacted positively to news of the potential agreement, though prices remain elevated compared to pre-conflict levels.

cards.headline: Consumer spending outpaces income growth as households draw down savings
cards.teaser: Americans are spending faster than their income is growing, drawing on savings to maintain consumption as energy prices rise.
cards.body:
Americans are spending at a rate that exceeds their income growth, increasingly relying on savings to support their purchases as the energy shock from the Iran war affects household budgets. The trend represents a shift in how consumers are managing their finances amid rising costs.

Consumer spending has remained steady despite low sentiment readings among households. Data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis shows the gap between spending and income growth is widening, creating questions about the sustainability of current consumption patterns as prices continue rising faster than household earnings.

cards.headline: Justice Department sues four states over denial of undercover plates for immigration officers
cards.teaser: The Justice Department filed lawsuits against Maine, Washington, Oregon, and Massachusetts for refusing to issue confidential license plates to federal agents.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice filed lawsuits Thursday against four states for refusing to issue undercover license plates to federal immigration officers. Maine, Washington, Oregon, and Massachusetts are targets of the legal action.

The DOJ argues that denying these confidential plates to federal agents interferes with law enforcement operations. The lawsuits follow an earlier letter from the Justice Department urging the four states to provide the plates to federal officers.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer rules out 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Governor Gretchen Whitmer said she will not run for president in 2028, removing a prominent Democrat from consideration.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not run for president in 2028. Whitmer, who is term-limited after winning two gubernatorial elections in the battleground state, had been widely viewed as a potential Democratic candidate.

The decision removes one of the Democratic Party's most prominent figures from the next presidential race. Whitmer's two election victories in Michigan, a key swing state, had positioned her as a strong potential contender for the nomination.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary appoints investor accused of anti-Islam remarks to Pentagon tech board
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth named Shaun Maguire, a venture capitalist accused of making remarks targeting New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to a Pentagon technology board.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth appointed Shaun Maguire, a Silicon Valley venture capitalist accused of making anti-Islam remarks about New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, to the Pentagon's Science, Technology and Innovation Board. Maguire is a partner at Sequoia Capital.

The Defense Department named Maguire along with 32 other appointees to the recently established board. The appointment comes amid controversy over statements Maguire allegedly made targeting Mamdani, who leads New York City.

cards.headline: AARP urges Congress to address Social Security solvency before trustees report
cards.teaser: AARP officials called on Congress to act on Social Security ahead of the annual trustees report from the Trump administration.
cards.body:
AARP officials are urging Congress to take action to ensure Social Security remains solvent ahead of the release of the annual board of trustees report from the Trump administration. The organization is calling for legislative measures to protect the program's long-term stability.

The trustees report, expected soon, will provide updated projections on Social Security's financial outlook. AARP officials stated they anticipate the report will show continued concerns about the program's future funding, though the exact release date and contents have not been announced.

cards.headline: Epstein survivors express doubts ahead of Pam Bondi House testimony
cards.teaser: Survivors say they have little faith Bondi's appearance before the House Oversight Committee will provide answers.
cards.body:
Survivors of Jeffrey Epstein expressed skepticism that Pam Bondi's scheduled testimony will produce meaningful answers about the case. Bondi is set to appear before the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

The hearing is scheduled to take place on Friday. Survivors have voiced concerns about whether the testimony will address their questions about Epstein's crimes and the handling of related investigations.
